title: Daily Signal Brief 049 — Article 50 T+1; four coordination clocks past Monday reactive-posture window
summary: Article 50 of the EU AI Act is enforceable as of Sunday 2 August 2026; today is T+1 and the Commission's enforcement press release IP/26/1714 landed Friday. Chatbots must disclose AI, deepfakes must be labelled, AI-generated content must carry machine-readable marks; fines up to €15M or 3% of worldwide turnover; about 190 organisations signed the Code of Practice by end of July. Monday 14:01Z reactive-posture discharge window closed empty on all three named Article 50 artefacts (Kernel v1.3 transparent-marking probe scope note; Compass /trust and /compare paragraph swap; Vector EU-buyer talking-point); Tuesday–Friday landings still discharge as T+1-to-T+5 catch-up with 'week one' framing truthful only if posted before Friday 7 August 14:01Z. Coordination triangle holds at four clocks with four-consecutive-dispatch stability: zero commits since 7/31 brief — twentieth revised-ETA null in twenty-six business days on the standing Tier 4 vehicle; Forge R1 verdict clock at eleven calendar / seven business days elapsed; Kernel v1.3 three full business days past Wednesday-due; Compass /trust and /compare one-half business day past Monday reactive. MCP mainline T+6 extends the T+3 devops/security-side anchoring set by Akamai and News4Hackers security-side reads; security-side now carries five independent enterprise-security reads and the story stabilizes as an enterprise-security-posture question, not just a devops-transport question. Bersin + HRTechFeed null pattern extends to fifth observation. Mobley Monday D+42 / D+30 passive-tail null; TA-lane 11-vendor 72h weekend + Monday scan null on any Article-50-aligned artefact filed at or across the general-application boundary — category-wide reactive-posture-across-boundary confirmed; Stratum's paragraph swap this week would be the earliest TA-lane vendor marker in Eglin's scan window.
